question: As announced on 24 April 2024 in its package of infringement decisions, the Commission has again written to Spain regarding the infringement procedure opened in 2021 ‒ initiated by the association En Colectivo ‒ on the compatibility of the extension of the AP-9 motorway concession with EU public procurement rules.

In its answer to my question E-002925/20231, the Commission stated that it had had several exchanges and meetings with the Spanish authorities. It seems that these were unsuccessful, as illustrated by this new letter of formal notice.

The Spanish Government’s decision to extend the concession for the AP-9 motorway infringes EU legislation, as the extension is equivalent to a new concession, which may be awarded only by means of a call for tenders. Spain has also failed to fulfil its obligations under EU public procurement rules, in particular Directive 93/37/EEC, as stated by the Commission.

The extension of the concession ‒ which the Galician Nationalist Bloc has repeatedly denounced in various institutions ‒ has the sole aim of benefiting the company Audasa. It has been a major scandal and has had a socioeconomic impact on the users of the motorway. The concession should therefore be withdrawn.
Can the Commission provide details of the latest developments in this matter and the Spanish Government’s response?
answer: The Commission sent an additional letter of formal notice to Spain under infringement procedure INFR(2021)4052 (1) on 24 April 2024, concerning the issue referred to by the Honourable Member. The Commission is now awaiting the response from the Spanish authorities, which is expected by 24 August 2024, upon their request to extend the initial deadline to reply by two months.

As indicated in the reply to Question E-002925/2023 (2), with a view to attaining an appropriate solution, the Commission is bound to maintain the confidentiality of the content of ongoing infringement procedures and cannot share any other detail at this stage.
